formulas.name: One-way ANOVA means model
formulas.expression: Y_ij = mu_i + eps_ij, eps_ij ~ N(0, sigma^2) and independent

symbols.Y_ij: j-th measurement for the i-th level of factor A

formulas.conditions: i=1,...,a; j=1,...,n; all populations normal with different means but same variance

formulas.name: One-way ANOVA effects model
formulas.expression: Y_ij = mu + tau_i + eps_ij, eps_ij ~ N(0, sigma^2) and independent, sum_{i=1}^{a} tau_i = 0

formulas.name: Group means and grand mean (dummy variable model)
formulas.expression: Ybar_i. = (1/n) sum_{j=1}^{n} Y_ij ; Ybar_.. = (1/a) sum_{i=1}^{a} Ybar_i. = (1/(a n)) sum_{i=1}^{a} sum_{j=1}^{n} Y_ij

formulas.name: SS_Total (one-way ANOVA)
formulas.expression: SS_Total = (Y - Ybar 1)^T (Y - Ybar 1) = sum_{i=1}^{a} sum_{j=1}^{n} (Y_ij - Ybar..)^2

formulas.name: SS_Error (one-way ANOVA)
formulas.expression: SS_Error = e^T e = (Y - Yhat)^T (Y - Yhat) = sum_{i=1}^{a} sum_{j=1}^{n} (Y_ij - Ybar_i.)^2

formulas.name: SS_Treatment (one-way ANOVA)
formulas.expression: SS_Treatment = SS_R = (Yhat - Ybar 1)^T (Yhat - Ybar 1) = n sum_{i=1}^{a} (Ybar_i. - Ybar..)^2

formulas.name: SS partition (one-way ANOVA)
formulas.expression: SS_Total = SS_Treatment + SS_Error

formulas.name: One-way ANOVA F test statistic
formulas.expression: F = [SS_Treatment / (sigma^2 (a-1))] / [SS_E / (sigma^2 a(n-1))] = MS_Treatment / MS_Error ~ F_{a-1, a(n-1)}
formulas.conditions: under H0; reject H0 when F > F_{1-alpha, a-1, a(n-1)}

formulas.name: Expected mean squares (one-way ANOVA)
formulas.expression: E[MS_Error] = sigma^2 ; E[MS_Treatment] = sigma^2 + (n/(a-1)) sum_{i=1}^{a} tau_i^2

formulas.name: ANOVA table template (single-factor experiment), Table 4.6
formulas.expression: Source: Treatments SS=SS_Treatments df=a-1 MS=MS_Treatments F0=MS_Treatments/MS_E ; Error SS=SS_E df=a(n-1) MS=MS_E ; Total SS=SS_T df=an-1

formulas.name: Residual definition (one-way ANOVA)
formulas.expression: e_ij = y_ij - yhat_ij = y_ij - ybar_i.

formulas.name: Effect size definition (coded 2^k design)
formulas.expression: [Q] = (gemiddelde respons bij Q=+1) - (gemiddelde respons bij Q=-1)

symbols.a,b,ab,(1): totals of n observations at the 4 design points of a 2^2 design

formulas.name: Contrasts for 2^2 design
formulas.expression: C_A = a + ab - b - (1) ; C_B = ab + b - a - (1) ; C_AB = ab + (1) - a - b

formulas.name: 2^3 effect estimate for A
formulas.expression: A = ybar_{A+} - ybar_{A-} = (1/(4n)) [a + ab + ac + abc - b - c - bc - (1)]

formulas.name: 2^3 effect estimate for B
formulas.expression: B = ybar_{B+} - ybar_{B-} = (1/(4n)) [b + ab + bc + abc - a - c - ac - (1)]

formulas.name: 2^3 effect estimate for C
formulas.expression: C = ybar_{C+} - ybar_{C-} = (1/(4n)) [c + ac + bc + abc - a - b - ab - (1)]

formulas.name: 2^3 effect estimate for AB
formulas.expression: AB = ybar_{AB+} - ybar_{AB-} = (1/(4n)) [ab + (1) + abc + c - b - a - bc - ac]

formulas.name: 2^3 effect estimate for AC
formulas.expression: AC = ybar_{AC+} - ybar_{AC-} = (1/(4n)) [ac + (1) + abc + b - a - c - ab - bc]

formulas.name: 2^3 effect estimate for BC
formulas.expression: BC = ybar_{BC+} - ybar_{BC-} = (1/(4n)) [bc + (1) + abc + a - b - c - ab - ac]

formulas.name: 2^3 effect estimate for ABC
formulas.expression: ABC = ybar_{ABC+} - ybar_{ABC-} = (1/(4n)) [abc - bc - ac + c - ab + b + a - (1)]

formulas.name: General effect formula for 2^k design
formulas.expression: Effect = Contrast / (n 2^{k-1})

formulas.name: General sum of squares formula for 2^k design
formulas.expression: SS = (Contrast)^2 / (n 2^k)

formulas.name: Standard error of an effect estimate (2^k design)
formulas.expression: s.e.(Effect) = sqrt( sigmahat^2 / (n 2^{k-2}) )

formulas.name: Approximate confidence interval on an effect (2^k design)
formulas.expression: Effect estimate +/- 2 [s.e.(effect)]
formulas.conditions: approximate 95% CI; if zero is contained, effect essentially zero / not significant at alpha=0.05

formulas.name: 2^(k-p) fraction size
formulas.expression: for a screening of k factors (each 2 levels) using only 2^r runs, you need a 2^{-k+r} = 2^{-p} fraction of the full factorial 2^k

formulas.name: Simple linear regression model
formulas.expression: Y = beta_0 + beta_1 x + epsilon

formulas.name: Multiple linear regression model
formulas.expression: Y = beta_0 + beta_1 x_1 + beta_2 x_2 + ... + beta_{p-1} x_{p-1} + epsilon

formulas.name: Mean and variance of Y given x (simple linear regression)
formulas.expression: mu_{Y|x} = E[Y|x] = beta_0 + beta_1 x ; Var[Y|x] = sigma^2
formulas.conditions: homoscedasticity: variance same for all x

formulas.name: Least squares objective
formulas.expression: L = sum_{i=1}^{n} eps_i^2 ; (beta0hat, beta1hat) = argmin_{beta0,beta1} sum_{i=1}^{n} (Y_i - beta_0 - beta_1 x_i)^2

formulas.name: Normal equations (simple linear regression)
formulas.expression: beta0hat = Ybar - beta1hat xbar (NE1) ; beta1hat = S_xY / S_xx (NE2)

formulas.name: Fitted regression line
formulas.expression: Yhat(x) = beta0hat + beta1hat x

formulas.name: SS_Total (regression)
formulas.expression: SS_Total = sum_{i=1}^{n} (Y_i - Ybar)^2
formulas.conditions: deviation of the data from their mean

formulas.name: SS_Error (regression)
formulas.expression: SS_Error = sum_{i=1}^{n} (Y_i - Yhat_i)^2
formulas.conditions: deviation of the data from the regression line; also written SS_E

formulas.name: SS_Regression
formulas.expression: SS_Regression = sum_{i=1}^{n} (Yhat_i - Ybar)^2
formulas.conditions: deviation of the regression line from the data mean

formulas.name: SS partition and R^2 (regression)
formulas.expression: SS_T = SS_R + SS_E ; R^2 = SS_R/SS_T = 1 - SS_E/SS_T

formulas.name: Degrees of freedom and expected SS (regression)
formulas.expression: SS_T has n-1 df, E[SS_T] = beta_1^2 S_xx + (n-1) sigma^2 ; SS_R has 1 df, E[SS_R] = beta_1^2 S_xx + sigma^2 ; SS_E has n-2 df, E[SS_E] = (n-2) sigma^2 ; SS_E/sigma^2 ~ Chi^2_{n-2}
formulas.conditions: if true model is Y_i=beta0+beta1 x_i+eps_i, eps_i~N(0,sigma^2)

formulas.name: Mean squares and variance estimate (regression)
formulas.expression: MS_R = SS_R/1 ; MS_E = SS_E/(n-2) ; sigmahat^2 = MS_E

formulas.name: Variance/covariance of coefficient estimators (simple regression)
formulas.expression: Var[beta0hat] = sigma^2 (1/n + xbar^2/S_xx) ; Var[beta1hat] = sigma^2/S_xx ; Cov[beta0hat, beta1hat] = -xbar sigma^2 / S_xx
formulas.conditions: beta0hat, beta1hat jointly normal, both independent of SS_E

formulas.name: t-test for slope
formulas.expression: (beta1hat - beta_{1,0}) / sqrt(MS_E/S_xx) ~ t_{n-2}

formulas.name: t-test for intercept
formulas.expression: (beta0hat - beta_{0,0}) / sqrt(MS_E (1/n + xbar^2/S_xx)) ~ t_{n-2}

formulas.name: F-test for significance of regression
formulas.expression: F = (MS_R/sigma^2) / ((n-2)MS_E/(sigma^2(n-2))) = MS_R/MS_E ~ F_{1,n-2}
formulas.conditions: under H0: beta1=0; Table 11-3 ANOVA layout: Regression SS_R df=1 MS_R F0=MS_R/MS_E; Error SS_E df=n-2 MS_E; Total SS_T df=n-1

formulas.name: Confidence interval for slope
formulas.expression: beta1hat + t_{alpha/2,n-2} sqrt(MS_E/S_xx) < beta1 < beta1hat + t_{1-alpha/2,n-2} sqrt(MS_E/S_xx)

formulas.name: Confidence interval for intercept
formulas.expression: beta0hat + t_{alpha/2,n-2} sqrt(MS_E (1/n + xbar^2/S_xx)) < beta0 < beta0hat + t_{1-alpha/2,n-2} sqrt(MS_E (1/n + xbar^2/S_xx))

formulas.name: Distribution of predicted mean response
formulas.expression: Yhat_0 ~ N( mu_{Y|x0}, sigma^2 (1/n + (xbar-x0)^2/S_xx) )

formulas.name: Confidence interval for mean response at x0
formulas.expression: Yhat_0 + t_{alpha/2,n-2} se(Yhat_0) <= mu_{Y|x0} <= Yhat_0 + t_{1-alpha/2,n-2} se(Yhat_0)

formulas.name: Prediction interval for a future observation at x0
formulas.expression: Yhat_0 + t_{alpha/2,n-2} se(e0) <= Y0 <= Yhat_0 + t_{1-alpha/2,n-2} se(e0)

formulas.name: Multiple linear regression model (population, k regressors)
formulas.expression: Y_i = beta_0 + beta_1 x_{1i} + beta_2 x_{2i} + ... + beta_k x_{ki} + eps_i, i=1,...,n

symbols.k+2: number of free parameters to estimate

formulas.name: Estimated response (multiple regression, k=2)
formulas.expression: Yhat = b0 + b1 X1 + b2 X2

formulas.name: R^2 (multiple regression)
formulas.expression: R^2 = SSR/SST
formulas.conditions: R^2 increases whenever a variable is added to the model

formulas.name: Adjusted R^2 (multiple regression)
formulas.conditions: only increases when an added variable is sufficiently significant; used to compare different models

formulas.name: Estimate of sigma (multiple regression)
formulas.expression: sigmahat = sqrt(MSE) = sqrt(SSE/(n-k-1))

formulas.name: Second-order polynomial model in two regressors
formulas.expression: Y = beta_0 + beta_1 x1 + beta_2 x2 + beta_12 x1 x2 + beta_11 x1^2 + beta_22 x2^2 + epsilon

formulas.name: F-test for a subset of regression coefficients
formulas.expression: F0 = { [SS_E(RM) - SS_E(FM)] / (k-r) } / { SS_E(FM) / (n-p) }
formulas.conditions: H0: beta_{r+1}=beta_{r+2}=...=beta_k=0 ; H1: at least one beta != 0

conventions.as_stated: If each group contains the same number of measurements, the experiment is balanced (we will always assume it is)

conventions.topic: Significance level (example-specific, no single stated course-wide default)
conventions.as_stated: Example 4.12 (paper tensile strength ANOVA) explicitly uses alpha=0.01 ('We will use alpha = 0.01'); separately, the 2^k effect confidence-interval rule references 'not significant at the alpha = 0.05 level'. The course does not state one single default alpha across this slice.

We hercoderen de levels altijd naar -1/+1 (recode factor levels to -1/+1); this is a translation and rescaling, all factors get the same 'schaal'; interaction columns also get -1/+1 levels as the product of the corresponding main-effect columns
[Q] = (gemiddelde respons bij Q=+1) - (gemiddelde respons bij Q=-1); no statement in this slice that effect = 2 x regression coefficient

conventions.topic: Aliasing and defining relation for fractional factorials
conventions.as_stated: The identity element I is also plus for the runs in the chosen fraction, therefore e.g. I = ABC is the defining relation; to find the aliases of a main effect or interaction, multiply the entire defining relation by that term (note: any column multiplied by itself always results in the identity column, i.e. A.A = I)

Resolution III designs: no main effects aliased with one another, main effects aliased with two-factor interactions. Resolution IV designs: no main effect aliased with any other main effect or two-factor interaction; two-factor interactions aliased with each other. Resolution V designs: no main effects or two-factor interactions aliased with each other; two-factor interactions aliased with three-factor interactions.

conventions.topic: Pooling higher-order interactions as error (single-replicate 2^k designs)
conventions.as_stated: For a large number of factors, say k>5, it is common practice to run only a single replicate of the 2^k design and pool or combine the higher-order interactions as estimate of error (illustrated for the nitride etch example by fitting model (A+B+C+D)^2, i.e. pooling 3-way and 4-way interactions into the error term)

Design generators should not be chosen arbitrarily. Choosing the incorrect design generator can result in a design of smaller resolution than possible. Select the design generators that will result in the highest possible design resolution.
the parameters mu_i and sigma^2 can be estimated using ordinary least-squares (OLS) estimation, which R/Excel/SPSS/Minitab/... can do

Check visually: do the residuals have constant variance? Are the residuals normally distributed? Make a normal probability plot, plot of residuals vs factor levels or vs treatment means. For regression: residuals vs fitted, residuals vs response, scale-location plot e_i/sqrt(sigmahat^2) (most values should be within (-2,2)), normal probability plot of residuals, residuals vs leverages.

conventions.topic: R^2 vs adjusted R^2 for model comparison
conventions.as_stated: R^2 always increases as more variables are added to the model (even if not significant); adjusted R^2 = 1-(1-R^2)(n-1)/(n-k-2) will only increase when the added variable is sufficiently significant, and is useful to compare different models: hoe hoger, hoe beter (the higher, the better)

conventions.topic: Significant figures / rounding when reporting regression coefficients
conventions.as_stated: Denk steeds na over het aantal beduidende cijfers dat je rapporteert. Excel trekt zich daar niets van aan, maar een ingenieur wel. (Always think about the number of significant digits you report. Excel does not care about this, but an engineer does.)
correlatie != causaliteit ('spurious' or 'confounding' relatie); a 'result' must also have practical meaning ('Resultaat' moet ook praktische betekenis hebben)
